<entry id="A03000">
<head-word>אַרְדָּא, </head-word>
<hw-number>I</hw-number>
<pos> m.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (Syr. ערדא, v. Löw Pfl. p. 303) 
<italic>mushroom, morel</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Keth. 61
<sup>a</sup> Ar. (ed. אַרְדֵּי pl.)—
<plural-form>Pl. אַרְדַּיָּא, אַרְדֵּי</plural-form>. Pes. 119
<sup>b</sup> ארדיא לי Ar. (ed. אַרְדְּלַיָּיא, אַרְדִּילַיָּא, אוּרְדִּילָאֵי, Ms. אַרְדִּילֵי, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note); Y. ib. X, end, 37
<sup>d</sup> ערדילו (read עַרְדִּילֵי or עַרְדֵּי לִי). Ber. 47
<sup>a</sup> ארדיא Ar. (ed. a. Ms. אַרְדִּילַיָּא). Ab. Zar. 38
<sup>a</sup> ארדי.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="A03026">
<head-word>אָרוּךְ</head-word>
<pos> m.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (ארך) </definition>
<notes/></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>long, tall, lasting;</italic> v. infra.</definition>
<notes> v. infra.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition> (= עָרוּךְ; cmp. אֲרִיךְ) 
<italic>well-arranged, well-balanced, thinker</italic>, a title of prominent scholars; cmp. אַרְיֹוךְ a. אֲרִיכָא.</definition>
<notes> [In legend intellectual eminence was identified with physical tallness.] Nidd. 24
<sup>b</sup> א' בדורו 
<italic>arukh</italic> (the tallest) in his generation. Kidd. 39
<sup>b</sup> עולם שכולו א' the world in which all is well-balanced (also called שכולו טוב) i.e. 
<italic>the hereafter.—Pl.</italic> אֲרוּכִים. Yoma 71
<sup>a</sup> חיים א' long life; a. fr.—Fem. אֲרוּכָה. Ber. I, 4 אחת א' one lengthy (benediction); a. fr.—Y. Hor. II, 46
<sup>d</sup> בא' by the long road, slowly; Shebu. 18
<sup>ab</sup>.—
<plural-form>Pl. אֲרוּכֹות</plural-form>. Y. Ber. II, 5
<sup>c</sup> top, a. e. א' וקצרות long and short roads, i.e. 
<italic>in all directions</italic>. V. next art.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<sup>a</sup>; ib. XXIII, 5 (151
<sup>b</sup>) א' המטה (some ed. ארובות, corr. acc.).—[Kel. XV, 2 א' של נחתומים Ar. Var.

<sup>b</sup> אין לך כל א' וא' וכ' there is no coffin in Palestine in which the Median horses do not eat straw (being used as cribs); a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. אֲרוֹנוֹת</plural-form>. Sot. 13
<sup>a</sup>; a. fr. [Y. Keth. VI, 30
<sup>d</sup> bot. וארון, v. אֲרִי I.]</notes></sense></senses></entry>
